rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry, so this is a conservative first candidate built from the contract physics rather than tuned values. Geometry: five sensors spaced 0.02 m apart across x = -0.04 to +0.04 m, all at y = 0.03 m ahead of the axle, so they see the line slightly before the wheels reach it. Sensor size 0.012 m is about half the 25 mm tape width, which gives a clear graded reading as the line moves across the array. Wheel track 0.12 m, wheel radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 x 0.18 m and mass 0.8 kg are mid-range values that keep yaw inertia moderate and the off-track limit at 0.06 m. Controller: sensor weights are proportional to sensor x (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), so the signal is positive when the line is left of centre and steers left, as the contract requires. kp = 2.0 gives a turn of about 700 PWM counts per unit of signal, which is firm but not saturating. kd = 0.3 damps the swing toward the line without adding much high-frequency noise. ki = 0 avoids integral windup on bends. base_speed = 1.6 (80 percent of full PWM) aims for the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in 3 s while leaving margin for cornering. line_loss = last_direction, so the robot keeps turning the way it was heading when the line is lost at the edge of a bend. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with rms error of a few millimetres and no line-loss events on gentle bends. The slalom may show oscillation or a small number of line losses. Next measurements: whether completion_time is under 3 s, where max_error peaks (which bend), and whether steering_oscillation is high enough to justify more kd or lower kp.
